title: PhD student in logistics and operational research
organization: Laboratoire de Génie Informatique, de Production et de Maintenance - University of Lorraine
subject: Integration of Blockchain in the Agricultural Supply Chain: Implications for Efficiency, Sustainability, and Finance
description:
My doctoral research focuses on the optimization of agricultural supply chains within an e-commerce context, leveraging blockchain technology to enhance transparency, traceability, efficiency, financial fairness, and environmental sustainability. The study addresses information asymmetry challenges in agri-food systems by proposing a blockchain-enabled supply chain architecture that secures transactions and improves trust among stakeholders.

The methodological framework combines game theory, robust optimization, and reinforcement learning to model multi-actor interactions, optimize logistics and financial performance, and enable adaptive decision-making. The research is validated through simulations and real-world data analysis, aiming to provide both theoretical contributions and practical solutions for sustainable and resilient agricultural supply chains.
